coverage: All 20 scenes: named cast, speaking minor roles, and named cultural references. Generic pronouns, unnamed crowds, ordinary oaths, places, and adjectival allusions are excluded.

entities.name: Prince Hamlet
entities.body: The prince of Denmark. Son of Gertrude and the recently deceased King Hamlet; nephew of the new king, Claudius.

entities.name: Claudius
entities.body: The new king of Denmark. Hamlet’s uncle, now married to Hamlet’s mother, Gertrude.

entities.name: Gertrude
entities.body: The queen of Denmark and Hamlet’s mother. Widow of the old king and now Claudius’s wife.

entities.name: Ophelia
entities.body: Polonius’s daughter and Laertes’s sister. Hamlet has been courting her.

entities.name: Polonius
entities.body: A senior adviser at the Danish court. Father of Ophelia and Laertes.

entities.name: Horatio
entities.body: Hamlet’s friend and a scholar from Wittenberg.

entities.name: Laertes
entities.body: Polonius’s son and Ophelia’s brother.

entities.name: The Ghost
entities.body: The mysterious apparition seen by the watchmen at Elsinore.
entities.identityNote: Keep the identity uncertain at first. A later card may report its claim to be Hamlet’s father after Act 1 Scene 5; never announce the murder accusation from the first appearance.

snapshots.body: The apparition seen by the watchmen at Elsinore, resembling Denmark’s dead king.
The apparition that identifies itself to Hamlet as his father’s spirit.

entities.name: King Hamlet
entities.body: Denmark’s recently deceased king. Prince Hamlet’s father and Gertrude’s first husband.

entities.name: Rosencrantz
entities.body: A friend of Hamlet from his youth, usually seen with Guildenstern.

entities.name: Guildenstern
entities.body: A friend of Hamlet from his youth, usually seen with Rosencrantz.

entities.name: Young Fortinbras
entities.body: A Norwegian prince. His father lost lands to Hamlet’s father in single combat.

entities.name: The elder Fortinbras
entities.body: The Norwegian ruler defeated by King Hamlet. Father of the young Fortinbras.

entities.name: The King of Norway
entities.body: Young Fortinbras’s uncle, the elderly ruler of Norway.

entities.name: Barnardo
entities.body: A soldier keeping watch at Elsinore, alongside Marcellus.

entities.name: Francisco
entities.body: The soldier whose watch Barnardo takes over at the opening.

entities.name: Marcellus
entities.body: A soldier at Elsinore, keeping watch with Barnardo.

entities.name: Voltemand
entities.body: A Danish courtier, paired with Cornelius as an envoy.

entities.name: Cornelius
entities.body: A Danish courtier, paired with Voltemand as an envoy.

entities.name: Reynaldo
entities.body: Polonius’s servant.

entities.name: The First Player
entities.body: An actor in the visiting company that Hamlet welcomes to Elsinore.

entities.name: The Player King
entities.body: The ruler in the play performed at court, also called Gonzago. A different figure from Claudius and Hamlet’s father.

entities.name: The Player Queen
entities.body: The ruler’s wife in the play performed at court, also called Baptista. A different figure from Gertrude.

entities.name: Lucianus
entities.body: A character in the play performed at court, introduced as the king’s nephew.

entities.name: The First Gravedigger
entities.body: The cemetery worker who jokes and debates while digging. Also labeled First Clown.

entities.name: The Second Gravedigger
entities.body: The First Gravedigger’s companion in the cemetery. Also labeled Second Clown.

entities.name: Osric
entities.body: An elaborately polite courtier at Elsinore.

entities.name: Yorick
entities.body: The late king’s jester, whom Hamlet knew as a child.

entities.name: Julius Caesar
entities.body: The Roman ruler invoked in Horatio’s comparison with ominous events in Denmark.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.body: The Roman god of the sea.
entities.editionNote: The opening modern-English passage explains the tides without naming Neptune; do not create a mention there.

entities.name: Jesus Christ
entities.body: Jesus Christ, the central figure of Christianity, also called the Saviour.
entities.editionNote: The opening modern-English passage says Christmas without naming the Saviour; do not create a mention there.

entities.name: The Norwegian captain
entities.body: An officer in Fortinbras’s army, whom Hamlet questions about the campaign.

entities.name: The court gentleman
entities.body: An unnamed courtier who brings news to the Danish royal household.

entities.name: The court lord
entities.body: An unnamed courtier who carries a message between the king and Hamlet.

entities.name: The sailor
entities.body: One of the sailors who bring Horatio a letter from Hamlet.

entities.name: The messenger
entities.body: An unnamed messenger carrying letters to the king.

entities.name: Horatio’s attendant
entities.body: The servant who announces visitors to Horatio.

entities.name: The priest
entities.body: The clergyman conducting the burial service.

entities.name: The English ambassador
entities.body: The spokesman for the ambassadors arriving from England.

entities.name: The Prologue
entities.body: The speaker who introduces the performance at court.

entities.name: Claudio
entities.body: A man who passes on the letters delivered to the king. The play gives little other information about him.

entities.name: Lamord
entities.body: A gentleman from Normandy, praised as a horseman and acquainted with Laertes.

entities.name: Yaughan
entities.body: The person to whom the gravedigger sends his companion to fetch a drink. His identity is not explained.

entities.name: Hyperion
entities.body: A sun god in Greek mythology, used in Hamlet’s comparison of his father and uncle.

entities.name: Niobe
entities.body: A grieving mother from Greek mythology, remembered for her tears.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The hero of classical mythology famed for his strength.

entities.name: The Nemean lion
entities.body: The formidable lion from the labors of Hercules.

entities.name: Saint Patrick
entities.body: The patron saint of Ireland, invoked in Hamlet’s oath.

entities.name: Roscius
entities.body: A celebrated actor of ancient Rome.

entities.name: Seneca
entities.body: The Roman writer of tragedies whom Polonius names while discussing theater.

entities.name: Plautus
entities.body: A Roman writer of comedies, paired with Seneca in Polonius’s account of the actors.

entities.name: Jephthah
entities.body: A biblical judge of Israel, the father in the ballad Hamlet quotes to Polonius.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.body: A Trojan hero who tells Dido about the fall of Troy in the speech Hamlet recalls.

entities.name: Dido
entities.body: The queen of Carthage, listening to Aeneas’s account of Troy.

entities.name: Priam
entities.body: The elderly king of Troy in the speech recited by the visiting actor.

entities.name: Pyrrhus
entities.body: A Greek warrior attacking Troy in the speech Hamlet asks the actor to recite.

entities.name: Hecuba
entities.body: The queen of Troy and Priam’s wife, portrayed in the actor’s speech.

entities.name: The Cyclopes
entities.body: The one-eyed giants of classical mythology, pictured here forging armor.

entities.name: Mars
entities.body: The Roman god of war.

entities.name: Fortune
entities.body: Luck imagined as a goddess who turns a wheel, raising people up and casting them down.

entities.name: Termagant
entities.body: A blustering figure from older popular drama, invoked as an example of overacting.

entities.name: Herod
entities.body: The biblical king as portrayed in older religious drama, notorious onstage for ranting.

entities.name: Vulcan
entities.body: The Roman god of fire and metalworking, imagined at his forge.

entities.name: Brutus
entities.body: The Roman conspirator associated with the killing of Julius Caesar.

entities.name: Phoebus
entities.body: A classical name for the sun god, imagined driving a chariot across the sky.

entities.name: Tellus
entities.body: The Roman goddess who personifies the earth.

entities.name: Hymen
entities.body: The classical god of marriage.

entities.name: Hecate
entities.body: A goddess associated with magic and witchcraft, invoked in the performed play.

entities.name: Damon
entities.body: A name Hamlet borrows from verse when addressing his friend Horatio.

entities.name: Nero
entities.body: The Roman emperor notorious for cruelty, including having his mother killed.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: Another name for Jupiter, king of the Roman gods.

entities.name: Mercury
entities.body: The messenger of the Roman gods.

entities.name: Saint Valentine
entities.body: The saint whose feast day appears in Ophelia’s song about lovers.

entities.name: Robin
entities.body: The beloved named in a song Ophelia sings; not a separately introduced courtier.

entities.name: Adam
entities.body: The first man in the biblical creation story, invoked in the gravediggers’ joke about digging.

entities.name: Cain
entities.body: The biblical son of Adam who killed his brother Abel.

entities.name: Alexander the Great
entities.body: The ancient Macedonian king and conqueror mentioned in Hamlet’s reflections on mortality.

entities.name: The sailors
entities.body: The sailors who carry Hamlet’s letter to Horatio.

entities.name: The English ambassadors
entities.body: The envoys arriving from England at the Danish court.

entities.name: The players
entities.body: The visiting company of actors welcomed by Hamlet.
